'''Jaylin Michael Williams''' (born June 29, 2002), nicknamed '''J-Will''', is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]]. A [[power forward]] / [[Center (basketball)|center]], he was selected by the Thunder in the second round of the [[2022 NBA draft]]. He is the first-ever NBA player of Vietnamese descent. Williams was a member of the Thunder's 2025 NBA championship team.

==Early life and family==
Jaylin Williams was born June 29, 2002<ref>{{cite web |title=Jaylin Michael Williams |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/player/298090/Jaylin-Michael-Williams |website=FIBA |access-date=June 23, 2022}}</ref> and grew up in [[Fort Smith, Arkansas]].<ref name="mussatto">{{cite web |last1=Mussatto |first1=Joe |date=January 26, 2023 |title=Thunder rookie Jaylin Williams has support of OKC's Vietnamese community |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/nba/thunder/2023/01/22/okc-thunder-jaylin-williams-nba-rookie-vietnamese-community-oklahoma-city-lunar-new-year/69828847007/ |access-date=March 9, 2024 |work=The Oklahoman}}</ref> Williams's parents are Michael and Linda Williams.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/nba/thunder/2025/05/07/who-is-jaylin-williams-get-to-know-okc-thunder-forward-from-arkansas/83505461007/|title=Who is Jaylin Williams? Get to know OKC Thunder forward from Arkansas|website=The Oklahoman|date=May 7, 2025}}</ref> Michael Williams was a high school basketball star in Fort Smith, Arkansas.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.essentiallysports.com/nba-active-basketball-news-who-are-jaylin-williams-parents-everything-to-know-about-michael-williams-and-linda-williams/|title=Who Are Jaylin Williams Parents? Everything To Know About Michael Williams And Linda Williams|first=Aayaan|last=Sayadee|date=May 17, 2025|website=Essentially Sports}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kark.com/good-news-matters/the-community-that-raised-jaylin-williams/|title=The community that raised Jaylin Williams |website=kark.com|last=Orange|first=Alyssa |date=March 22, 2022}}</ref> He is African-American.<ref name="auto"/> Linda Williams was born in Saigon (now [[Ho Chi Minh City]]), [[South Vietnam]] and moved to the United States in [[Fall of Saigon|1975]] after the [[Vietnam War]].<ref name="mussatto" />A teacher, Linda Williams grew up in Hammond, Indiana.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://andscape.com/features/oklahoma-city-thunder-center-jaylin-williams-making-history-in-nba-finals/|title=Oklahoma City Thunder center Jaylin Williams making history in NBA Finals|last=Spears|first=Marc|website=Andscape|date=June 9, 2025}}</ref>

==High school career==
Williams played basketball for [[Northside High School (Fort Smith, Arkansas)|Northside High School]] in [[Fort Smith, Arkansas]], where he played with his future NBA teammate, [[Isaiah Joe]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Allen |first1=Nate |title=Fort Smith Northside duo contribute big at Arkansas |url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2021/nov/27/fort-smith-northside-duo-contribute-big-at/ |work=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]] |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=November 27, 2021}}</ref> As a sophomore, he helped his team reach the Class 7A state final.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Dawson |first1=Dudley E. |title=Fort Smith Northside's Williams continues sprouting up |url=https://www.wholehogsports.com/news/2018/apr/07/fort-smith-northsides-williams-continues-sprouting/?f=recruiting |publisher=WholeHogSports |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=April 7, 2018}}</ref> In his junior season, Williams averaged 16 points, 11 rebounds and three blocks per game,<ref name="bio">{{cite web |title=Jaylin Williams |date=July 6, 2020 |url=https://arkansasrazorbacks.com/roster/jaylin-williams/ |publisher=Arkansas Razorbacks |access-date=June 13, 2022}}</ref> and was named Arkansas Division I Player of the Year by the ''Northwest Arkansas Democrat-Gazette''.<ref>{{cite web |title=DI Boys Player of the Year: Jaylin Williams • FS Northside |url=https://www.nwaonline.com/news/2019/apr/07/di-boys-player-year-jaylin-williams-fs-northside/ |work=[[The Northwest Arkansas Times]] |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=April 7, 2019}}</ref> He led his team to the Class 6A state title and was named tournament MVP after recording 20 points and 16 rebounds in the title game.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Taylor |first1=Erick |title='Humble' Northside earns respect |url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2019/mar/09/humble-northside-earns-respect-20190309/ |work=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]] |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=March 9, 2019}}</ref> As a senior, Williams averaged 18.7 points, 12.2 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 2.5 blocks per game, earning Arkansas [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] honors and repeating as Arkansas Division I Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Williams named Gatorade Arkansas Player of the Year |url=https://www.swtimes.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2020/03/27/williams-named-gatorade-arkansas-player/1451816007/ |work=[[Southwest Times Record]] |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=March 27, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Boyd |first1=Paul |title=All-NWADG Basketball: Williams expands game looking to college |url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2020/mar/27/all-nwadg-division-i-boys-basketball-wi/ |work=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]] |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=March 27, 2020}}</ref> A consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for the University of [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] over an offer from [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], among other programs.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Davenport |first1=Richard |title=Fort Smith Northside's Jaylin Williams commits to Arkansas |url=https://www.nwaonline.com/news/2019/nov/23/big-man-jaylin-williams-commits-arkansas/ |work=[[The Northwest Arkansas Times]] |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=November 23, 2019}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman at the University of Arkansas, Williams averaged 3.7 points and 4.7 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Jones |first1=Taylor |title=Jaylin Williams Deserves More Respect |url=https://razorbackswire.usatoday.com/2022/03/02/jaylin-williams-deserves-more-respect/ |publisher=Razorbacks Wire |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=March 2, 2022}}</ref> He became a regular starter in his sophomore season.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Collier |first1=Jackson |title=2021-22 Season in Review: Jaylin Williams |url=https://arkansas.rivals.com/news/2021-22-season-in-review-jaylin-williams |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=May 21, 2022}}</ref> Williams averaged 10.9 points and 9.8 rebounds per game, receiving first-team All-[[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) honors from the league's coaches. He was a second-team All-SEC selection by the [[Associated Press]] and made the All-Defensive Team.<ref name=bio/> Williams led the [[NCAA Division I]] with 54 [[charge (basketball)|charges]] drawn and grabbed 364 rebounds, setting a program single-season record. He [[NBA draft declaration|declared for the NBA draft]] and opted to forgo his remaining college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Whaley |first1=Logan |title=Jaylin Williams staying in NBA Draft, will not return to Arkansas |url=https://www.ky3.com/2022/05/30/jaylin-williams-staying-nba-draft-will-not-return-arkansas/ |publisher=KY3 |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=May 30, 2022}}</ref>

==Professional career==

Williams was selected by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in the second round of the [[2022 NBA draft]] with the 34th overall pick,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://okcthunderwire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/thunder/2022/06/23/2022-nba-draft-thunder-select-jaylin-williams-at-no-34/77343162007/|title=2022 NBA draft: Thunder select Jaylin Williams at No. 34|first=Clemente|last=Almanza|website=OKC Thunder Wire}}</ref> becoming the first player of Vietnamese descent to be drafted in the NBA.<ref>{{cite news|first=Sarah|last=Coleman|title=Jaylin Williams Picked by the Oklahoma City Thunder in NBA Draft|date=June 24, 2022|work=About You|url=https://www.aymag.com/jaylin-williams-ok-city-thunder/|access-date=June 25, 2022}}</ref> Earlier in the same draft, the Thunder selected the similarly-named [[Jalen Williams]]. Fans and teammates have taken to calling Jaylin Williams by the nickname "J-Will" and calling Jalen Williams by the nickname "J-Dub" as a means of differentiation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=OKC Thunder |date=2022-06-25 |title=just to be clear: J-Dub = Jalen Williams (Santa Clara) J-Will = Jaylin Williams (Arkansas) |url=https://x.com/okcthunder |access-date=2025-06-29 |website=X}}</ref>

A [[power forward]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.koco.com/article/jalen-williams-wrist-surgery-nba-okc-thunder/65251321|title=Thunder's Jalen Williams to undergo wrist surgery|first=Jonathan|last=Greco|date=June 30, 2025|website=KOCO}}</ref> Williams joined the Thunder's [[2022 NBA Summer League]] team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oklahoma City Thunder 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612760/thunder |access-date=2022-07-21 |website=nba.com}}</ref> In his Summer League debut, he scored two points and six rebounds in a 98–77 win against the [[Utah Jazz]] in the [[Salt Lake City]] Summer League.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oklahoma City Thunder vs Utah Jazz Jul 5, 2022 Box Scores |url=https://www.nba.com/game/okc-vs-uta-1622200002/box-score#box-score |access-date=2022-07-21 |website=www.nba.com}}</ref> On July 19, 2022, Williams signed with the Thunder.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Thunder Signs Second-Round Pick Jaylin Williams |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/signs-jaylin-williams-220719 |access-date=2022-07-21 |website=www.nba.com}}</ref>

In October 2024, Williams suffered a right hamstring strain which left him out of the remainder of preseason.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lorenzi |first1=Joel |date=October 3, 2024 |title=Jaylin Williams injury update: OKC Thunder forward out for preseason with hamstring strain |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/nba/thunder/2024/10/03/jaylin-williams-injury-update-okc-thunder-forward-out-for-preseason/75502975007/ |access-date=4 October 2024 |website=The Oklahoman}}</ref> Williams returned to active play on December 23.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Styles |first1=Rylan |date=December 23, 2024 |title=OKC Thunder Excited To Have Jaylin Williams Back in Fold, For Good Reason |url=https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/news/okc-thunder-excited-to-have-jaylin-williams-back-in-fold-for-good-reason |access-date=11 February 2025 |work=Oklahoma City Thunder on SI |publisher=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> On March 7, Williams recorded his first career triple-double with 10 points, 11 rebounds, and 11 assists in a 107–89 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Styles |first=Rylan |date=March 7, 2025 |title=OKC Thunder Reserve Notches Triple Double Against Trail Blazers |url=https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/news/okc-thunder-jaylin-williams-notches-triple-double-trail-blazers-march-7 |access-date=March 7, 2025 |work=Oklahoma City Thunder on SI |publisher=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> On March 19, Williams recorded his second career triple-double with 19 points, 17 rebounds, and 11 assists in a 133–100 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. He also joined [[Russell Westbrook]], [[Kevin Durant]], [[Josh Giddey]], and [[Shai Gilgeous-Alexander]] as the only players to record multiple triple-doubles in Thunder franchise history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/oklahoma-city-thunder/thunder-news-jaylin-williams-immediate-reaction-career-night-76ers|title=Thunder center Jaylin Williams' immediate reaction to career night vs. 76ers|work=ClutchPoints|last=Pavon|first=Josue|date=March 20, 2025|access-date=March 21, 2025}}</ref>

On June 22, 2025, Williams won an NBA championship when the Thunder defeated the Indiana Pacers 103–91 in Game 7 of the NBA Finals.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Feldscher |first=Jacob Lev, Kevin Dotson, Issy Ronald, Jamie Barton, Kyle |date=2025-06-22 |title=The Oklahoma City Thunder win the NBA championship after defeating Indiana Pacers in winner-take-all Game 7 |url=https://www.cnn.com/sport/live-news/nba-finals-game-7-pacers-thunder-spt |access-date=2025-06-27 |work=CNN}}</ref>

On June 29, 2025, his 23rd birthday, Williams signed a three-year, $24 million contract extension with the Thunder.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.nba.com/news/thunder-sign-jaylin-williams-to-multi-year-extension |title=Thunder sign Jaylin Williams to multi-year extension |website=NBA.com |date=June 29, 2025 |access-date=June 29, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-williams-250629 |title=Thunder Signs Jaylin Williams to Multi-Year Contract Extension |website=NBA.com |date=June 29, 2025 |access-date=June 29, 2025}}</ref>

Williams is the first player of Vietnamese descent to play in the NBA and to win an NBA championship.<ref name="mussatto"/> He is the last player in NBA history to wear jersey number 6. The number 6 was retired league-wide in 2022 following former player [[Bill Russell]]'s death that year.<ref>{{cite web |last=Aker |first=Nate |date=October 4, 2025 |title=Jaylin Williams Expresses Gratitude Toward NBA Hall-of-Famer |url=https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/onsi/news/jaylin-williams-expresses-gratitude-toward-nba-hall-of-famer-01k6jggxs0kc |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=December 3, 2025}}</ref>
